layer1_philosophy.methodology: Explicit, systematic phonics and word study taught through a fixed workshop cycle, with repeated application to connected reading and writing
principles: Teach phonics, syllable types, spelling patterns, and morphology in a deliberate sequence that builds on previous learning.
Keep instruction active and brief, then spend substantial time applying the weekly word pattern in authentic connected text and writing.
Use a review-and-repetition cycle across several weeks, with cumulative checks, so a newly introduced pattern is not mistaken for mastery.
Differentiate the application text rather than withholding grade-level instruction: every week pairs an Accountable Text with a simpler Interactive Text for extra support.
Make thinking about words public through word sorts, partner talk, context clues, dictation, and reflection instead of relying on isolated worksheets alone.

evidence.quote: phonics and word study instruction must be explicit and systematic
applying new skills in real reading and writing experiences
review-and-repetition cycle over extended periods of time to ensure mastery
whole-group mini-lessons, small-group instruction, independent work, and assessments
can be implemented with other Benchmark Workshop modules or stand on its own

layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: systematic-sequential instruction with spiral review, explicit modeling, guided application, and mastery informed by cumulative evidence
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: A spelling pre-assessment opens each week, a spelling-pattern assessment closes it, a cumulative unit assessment at the end of Week 3 revisits current and prior skills, and the separate Quick Phonics and Quick Spelling Assessments are intended for fall, winter, and spring diagnostic checks.
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: Act as the teacher: introduce the pattern explicitly, listen during passage reading, prompt the child to cite the text, model context and decoding strategies, give corrective feedback, adapt the support text when needed, and use cumulative evidence to decide review rather than treating one weekly score as mastery.

knowledgeBankMatches.note: The Stairway to Reading proposal uses explicit sequencing, repetition, and mastery checks, but it is a one-to-one remedial program. Benchmark is a Grade 3 core workshop with whole-group, small-group, and differentiated connected-text application, so it needs its own scoped entry rather than inheriting the remediation format.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark systematic phonics and word study
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: An explicit Grade 3 word-study approach that sequences phonics, syllable types, spelling patterns, and morphology, then applies each weekly target in connected reading, writing, sorting, dictation, and cumulative review.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Teach one word pattern at a time through explicit correspondence or word-study instruction, automaticity practice, a grade-level Accountable Text, a simpler Interactive Text for extra support, word sorting, dictation, writing after reading, repeated reading, and assessment. Review skills across later weeks and use cumulative evidence to decide whether learning transferred. Preserve grade-level exposure while changing the support text and amount of modeling for children who need it.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark Grade 3 phonics and word study workshop format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A 10-unit, 30-week workshop. Every week uses five lessons: introduce and pre-assess, read a grade-level passage, reread and write, read a simpler support passage, then review and assess.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Organize the year as 10 three-week units. Each week targets one phonics, syllable, spelling, or morphology pattern. Lesson 1 introduces the pattern, builds automaticity, and pre-assesses spelling. Lesson 2 reads an Accountable Text and uses context clues and a closed sort. Lesson 3 rereads for fluency, writes about the text, completes dictation, and sorts by common features. Lesson 4 uses a simpler Interactive Text, multisyllabic decoding, buddy sorting, and high-frequency-word review. Lesson 5 rereads, decodes by analogy, assesses spelling, extends learning, and contributes to the cumulative unit check.

layer3_structure.cadence: Five lessons per week for 30 weeks, organized as 10 units of three weeks each. Lessons 1 to 3 are the main whole-group sequence; Lessons 4 and 5 are a smaller-group extra-support sequence that uses the simpler Interactive Text.

sessionLengthMinutes.note: The guide gives component durations, commonly two to five minutes, but does not state one reliable total for the full daily lesson. Homa should preserve the short-component rhythm without inventing a total duration.

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Lesson 1: introduce the sound-spelling, syllable, or morphology target, build automaticity, pre-assess spelling, and reflect. Lesson 2: read the grade-level Accountable Text, use context clues, complete a closed sort, and reflect. Lesson 3: reread for fluency, discuss before writing, write a follow-up, complete dictation, and sort by common features. Lesson 4: read the simpler Interactive Text, apply the Reading Big Words Strategy, complete a buddy sort, review high-frequency words, and build fluency. Lesson 5: reread the support text, decode by analogy, assess the week's spelling pattern, review high-frequency words, extend learning, and contribute to the cumulative unit assessment.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: Linear sequence with spiral review and cumulative mastery evidence. The weekly target advances in order, but current and prior patterns remain in later fluency and assessment work for four to six weeks.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Every week begins with a pre-assessment and ends with a spelling-pattern assessment. Every third week closes with a cumulative unit assessment of current and previously taught skills. The separate Quick Phonics and Quick Spelling Assessments are designed for fall, winter, and spring administration.
layer3_structure.notes: The workshop is written for a classroom and repeatedly refers to partners, whole groups, small groups, and differentiated readers. In a homeschool setting, the parent can keep the same instructional sequence but replace partner turns with parent-child talk and choose between the Accountable and Interactive Text based on observed reading support needs.

activityTypes.sourceQuote: Word Sorts to deepen students’ awareness of common spelling patterns

activityTypes.description: A weekly pre-assessment, end-of-week spelling-pattern check, and cumulative unit check monitor current and earlier skills.
Short literal, inferential, evidence-finding, and personal-response questions follow each Accountable or Interactive Text.
Differentiated lists of simpler and multisyllabic words are reread across the week to build automatic recall without framing the task as speed reading.
activityTypes.sourceQuote: Build Automaticity activities for fluency building

suggestedRecipe.name: word-fluency-speed-drill
suggestedRecipe.description: A parent-facing repeated-reading sheet with two difficulty bands, a small observation table for accuracy and smoothness across attempts, and explicit language that the goal is automaticity rather than racing.

activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-02 through GAP_ALIASES: word-fluency-speed-drill maps to word-fluency-repeated-reading. The shared recipe keeps the validated word set stable across warm rereading rounds, separates the child page from parent observations, and refuses generated seconds targets, words-per-minute goals, pass lines, or progression thresholds. It copies no source list, band name, sequence, timing, script, or page geometry.

activityTypes.description: A compact instructional chart names the target pattern, shows representative words, and remains available during reading and writing.

suggestedRecipe.name: phonics-pattern-reference-chart
suggestedRecipe.description: A one-page reference with one target sound or morphology rule, a small set of validated example words grouped by spelling, and a parent note for using it during real reading and writing.

activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-02: shipped phonics-pattern-reference-chart with one trusted taught skill id, a closed example blueprint, deterministic word, group, and literal target-span validation, and original Homa geometry. It preserves no source chart title, examples, categories, order, color system, wording, or visual identity.

activityTypes.description: Cut-apart cards support rapid review of current and previously taught high-frequency words.

suggestedRecipe.name: high-frequency-word-card-deck
suggestedRecipe.description: Large cut-apart word cards from a supplied, age-appropriate word list, with restrained card backs and a short parent routine for retrieval practice in both directions.

activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-02 through GAP_ALIASES: high-frequency-word-card-deck maps to flash-cards because the reusable physical and retrieval procedure is identical. The shared recipe accepts one closed trusted word set and explicitly excludes the source's word list, order, categories, card backs, colors, routines, and visual design.

activityTypes.description: The parent dictates words and sentences for guided spelling, then the child discusses and writes a brief response to the week's passage.

suggestedRecipe.name: dictation-writing-practice
suggestedRecipe.description: A two-part page with parent-only dictated words and one original sentence, closed answer guidance, then a short talk-to-write response box tied to the child’s just-read passage.

activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-02: shipped dictation-writing-practice as a three-page child, parent-guide, and answer-key packet. Exact items, answers, accepted variants, target spans, and any scoring or timing policy stay deterministic; the optional talk-to-write response remains open and unscored. It copies no source list, sentence, passage, question, script, threshold, order, or layout.

layer5_lessons.notes: All 30 weekly targets and all 60 titled Accountable and Interactive Texts are decomposed from the three-part capture. This remains partial under the Layer 5 honesty rule because the source defines five daily lessons per week, while this pass records the complete week-to-skill and week-to-text map rather than 150 daily rows. Volume 1 supplies Units 1 to 5. The captured Volume 2 stops during Unit 8, Week 2 and contains no teacher-guide pages for the rest of Unit 8 or Units 9 to 10. The Word Study Resource Book still supplies exact targets and both titled texts for all 30 weeks, so the missing daily teacher pages do not create a gap in the week-to-work index. Questions are not invented: two captured Unit 8 examples are recorded, and the rest remain empty until a future daily-lesson pass has the corresponding teacher page.

decisionsNeeded.impact: The current capture fully supports curriculum routing, 30-week planning, and story-title search. A complete 150-lesson prompt-and-question decomposition remains awaiting source; the request receipt is Slack reply 1785643625.555959 in thread 1785552891.449889.

The existing English phonics, spelling, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing topics cover the instructional scope. Unit themes are mapped as partial context so Homa does not confuse a phonics passage with a full science or civics lesson.

notes: A complete 300-page, three-part capture: Volume 1, Volume 2, then the Word Study Resource Book. The files contain a core Grade 3 phonics and word-study workshop, not a general reading anthology. Its standout reusable pattern is a weekly pair of short connected texts, one grade-level Accountable Text and one simpler Interactive Text, used to apply the same word pattern at two support levels. Alessa's Slack comment called out the great simple short stories; all 60 titles are now searchable by week. The analysis does not turn incidental animals, robots, weather, or story characters into whole-curriculum subjects. Those themes remain attached to the relevant weekly works and contextual Layer 2 mappings.
